tasks.title: Exclusive vault lock
requirements: OpLog.open takes the lock before anything else: before it reads the manifest, truncates a torn tail, rewrites manifest.json or opens a segment for append. The lock is the file .memev/oplog/LOCK, created with an exclusive create (flag wx), written with pid, host, boot id (the boot time computed from os.uptime()), the holder's own start time, read for its pid from the same source that judges a lock (the /proc or /bin/ps read of requirement 14), a per-boot machine identifier and a random token, and fsynced; its bytes never change while it is held
a second opener gets a VaultLocked error naming the holder pid

a read-only open (new Vault(root, { readOnly: true }) and new OpLog(dir, { readOnly: true })) takes no lock and writes nothing: no recover() import, no torn-tail truncate, no manifest, snapshot, device, index or graph write, no bus seeding and no commit; it reads a torn tail as absent, and log.append() on it throws

the lock test opens the second writable Vault from a child process, the way memev claims does (src/cli/main.mjs:327), and asserts VaultLocked with the active segment, manifest.json, snapshot.json and device.json byte-identical; OpLog.open never writes snapshot.json, so an unchanged snapshot alone proves nothing

a lock is stale only when: on the same host, the same boot and the same per-boot machine identifier (linux /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, darwin /usr/sbin/sysctl -n kern.bootsessionuuid, read without PATH; boot times from os.uptime() within 120 s), compared together with the pid namespace before any pid rule, its pid is not alive, or is alive with a start time more than 2 s from the recorded one (pid reuse), or equals the reader's own pid while the reader holds no token for it (an earlier run in a restarted container); on another host or boot, the lock file's mtime is more than 90 s old. An empty or unparsable lock is held while its mtime is younger than 60 s and stale after. When a pid's start time cannot be read (Windows, or the read fails), the holder counts as alive, and memev doctor names the lock's pid, host and age so the owner can remove it once that process is gone. Node core has no flock or fcntl and Memev takes no dependency, so no OS advisory lock is used

the holder renews the lock every 15 s from a worker_threads worker by setting its mtime to now (fs.utimesSync) after checking that the lock still carries its token; the lock's bytes never change, and a main thread blocked in a long synchronous verify keeps the lock; MEMEV_LOCK_RENEW_MS shortens the interval for tests; clocks may differ between hosts by up to 60 s; before every write to the oplog folder (append, snapshot, manifest write, roll, archive and close) the holder checks that the lock still carries its token and fails closed with VaultLocked if it does not; a holder that lost the lock never renews, rewrites or deletes a lock that is not its own

stale recovery takes a recovery mutex, .memev/oplog/LOCK.recover, with an exclusive create, re-reads LOCK inside it and goes on only if LOCK's bytes still equal the stale lock it judged; only then does it rename the stale lock away and create its own LOCK with wx, releasing the mutex last; a live lock is never moved, so LOCK always exists while its holder runs; a mutex older than 10 s whose writer is not alive is itself stale; two openers recovering the same stale lock never both hold the vault
any error other than EEXIST while creating the lock (EACCES, ENOSPC, EROFS) fails the open with that error; it is never read as a held or a stale lock
a second writable open in the process that holds the lock is refused with VaultLocked like any other; the lock is never re-entrant
VaultLocked is exported from src/engine/oplog.mjs, and a bare new OpLog(dir).open() takes the lock too
on Linux the lock also records the pid namespace (readlink /proc/self/ns/pid), and a lock from another pid namespace counts as another host
a process's record of the locks it holds is keyed by the real path of the oplog folder (fs.realpathSync), so a symlink, a trailing slash or a '..' spelling of the same vault is the same lock

MEMEV_LOCK_TEST_PAUSE=after-judge:<ms> pauses a recoverer after it judges a lock stale and before it touches LOCK or the mutex, and after-rename:<ms> right after it renames a stale lock away, for tests
a pid's start time is read from /proc/<pid>/stat on Linux and from /bin/ps -o lstart= -p <pid> run with TZ=UTC and LC_ALL=C on macOS, never through PATH

T1 also turns the runner's two writable opens (src/cli/runner.mjs, in the command and in watch) into daemon calls or read-only opens, so test/runner.test.mjs and the full suite pass on T1's own commit; T2 then adds its criteria on top
a holder that lost the lock writes nothing on close: no index, graph, device or devices file, and no commit
the T1 tests also run in a linux container, so the linux-only branches (the /proc start time, the pid namespace, the boot id) run on a gate that is not linux

tasks.title: The daemon and the CLI openers live with the lock
requirements: the daemon's start (src/server/main.mjs) meets a held lock with exit code 5 (code 4 already means it cannot listen) within 2 s, a VaultLocked message naming the holder's pid, and no daemon.lock left behind; it never ends in an uncaught error
memev start (startDaemon, src/cli/daemon.mjs) reports exit code 5 as the vault being locked by that pid, not as 'did not start'

memev claims uses the daemon over HTTP when it is up and a read-only open when it is not; memev doctor without --fix opens read-only; memev compact takes the lock and, with a live holder, refuses with VaultLocked naming its pid and saying to stop it first; memev doctor --fix with a live daemon repairs over HTTP and by restart as it does today, writes no record to .memev/oplog from the CLI, and names any oplog fix it cannot apply as needing the daemon stopped, with VaultLocked and the daemon's pid
compact's guard is the lock, not daemon.json
a daemon that cannot listen closes its vault, releasing the lock, before it exits with code 4

a daemon whose token check, made by the renew worker at every renewal and before every write, finds the lock taken by another holder exits with the VaultLocked code within 2 s, and its supervisor waits for the holder (requirement on the login units), instead of answering /healthz while it refuses writes
memev doctor names a held lock's pid, host and age in seconds and exits non-zero, and reports a lock whose holder is gone as stale and recoverable
the login units do not restart a daemon refused by a held lock every few seconds: systemd's unit carries RestartPreventExitStatus=5, and launchd's plist sets ThrottleInterval to at least 60
